question.text: As per Regulation 15A of the SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, a research analyst is entitled to charge fees for providing research services from:

answer.text: A client, including an accredited investor, in the manner specified by SEBI
Only retail clients, with fees capped at a flat amount set by the exchange
Only the issuer companies whose securities are being researched
Only the stockbroker through whom the client transacts

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 15A of the SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations explicitly entitles a research analyst to charge fees for providing research services from a client, including an accredited investor, in the manner specified by SEBI. This grounds the analyst's fee-charging right in a defined client relationship governed by SEBI-specified terms. The Trap: The regulation does not limit charging only to retail clients, does not route fees through the broker, and does not allow charging the issuers being researched (which would create a clear conflict). The "in the manner specified by SEBI" phrase is what governs how the fee may be charged. Note: The NISM Series XV (Research Analyst) workbook supports the factual right to charge fees from a client including an accredited investor under Regulation 15A, but the surrounding "purpose" framing about reducing brokerage dependence or implementing a MiFID-style unbundling model was not located in the workbook pages reviewed. The framing above is presented as the directly source-supported factual statement of the rule.
